correctness.rationale: For Q=D^T L^+ D with D carrying square roots of conductances, the eigenvalues of L on class-centered vectors and on the class difference are n(1+x²) and 2nx², respectively. Using their reciprocals gives the internal-source sums and the cross-source types according to zero, one or two matching endpoints. Only the zero-match cross current changes sign, at x=1. The P column sum equals the Q sum plus 1 minus twice the Q diagonal, since the latter is in [0,1]. Symmetry gives the same real induced 1 and infinity norms. I checked the factored orbit comparisons: the weak-cross cycle factor (n²−4n+2)x+n²−6n+2 is negative for n=3,4, is 7x−3 for n=5, and positive for n>=6; the strong-cross differences are strictly positive even at the smallest allowed n. Comparing z>1 to 1/z strictly improves the internal branch in both norms and improves the weak cross cycle branch except for exact equality at n=3. On x>=1 each cross maximum is the top Rayleigh quotient of the corresponding symmetric 2-by-2 matrix with off-diagonal coefficient half the numerator's linear coefficient; its positive maximizing ratio exceeds 1 and solves x−1/x=4(n−1)/n for Q or 4(n−2)/n for P. Thus x=1 is not a global maximizer; only the n=3 cycle branch has the additional reciprocal optimizer. The quotient values give the stated finite-n maxima and are strictly below their n→∞ limits, proving both sharp suprema.
residual_risks: The conclusion is for equal communities, positive conductances, canonical Euclidean-orthogonal projections and unweighted coordinate endpoint norms. The finite checks are corroboration only, not the proof of the optimizers or suprema.

originality.rationale: The weighted transfer-current operator is standard, and reentrance already occurs in another indexed weighted family. The supported distinct claim is the exact two-equal-clique positive-cross-conductance classification, with its n=5 crossover, n=3 reciprocal cycle optimum, and sharp finite-size and uniform optimizations. The strongest inspected localization theorems and indexed exact formulas do not provide these by specialization.
residual_risks: The strongest indexed analogy shares the method and the reentrant phenomenon; no verified reduction supplies the exact new graph family. Less-indexed equivalent network computations may exist. Bounded searches do not establish priority.

value.rationale: The two-community complete network is a natural weighted test family, and a closed norm bound alone would conceal the change in maximizing type. In particular one size has an extra cycle phase while the smallest size has two distinct maximizing conductances. Exact comparisons and uniform sharp bounds therefore give structural information about coordinate amplification in the canonical projections, not just a list of example calculations.
residual_risks: No general claim about arbitrary conductance models, projection constants or intermediate norms follows.
